intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor variable declarations in gve_get_ethtool_stats to improve clarity regarding RX/TX statistics indices and lengths.
intent_record.what: Replaced generic integer variable declarations (base_stats_idx, max_stats_idx) with specific RX/TX variants (rx_base_stats_idx, max_rx_stats_idx, max_tx_stats_idx) and introduced new length variables (stats_region_len, nic_stats_len) within gve_get_ethtool_stats.
intent_record.how: Improves code clarity and maintainability by explicitly distinguishing between receive and transmit statistic indices and defining required length parameters, without altering the underlying execution logic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Added alignment validation guard for NIC stats region boundaries with improved variable separation for RX/TX statistics tracking
intent_record.what: Replaced single base_stats_idx/max_stats_idx variables with separate rx_base_stats_idx, max_rx_stats_idx, max_tx_stats_idx variables; added stats_region_len and nic_stats_len calculations; introduced alignment validation check with net_err_ratelimited() error logging; updated loop to use rx_base_stats_idx
intent_record.how: Adds runtime validation to ensure NIC stats region starts at a multiple of stats size boundary; prevents potential out-of-bounds access or incorrect stats mapping by catching alignment mismatches early; separates RX and TX statistics index tracking for clearer boundary management between driver and NIC stats

intent_record.intent_summary: Fixes stats report buffer allocation size by using maximum configured queue counts instead of current active counts.
intent_record.what: Replaced gve_num_tx_queues(priv) with priv->tx_cfg.max_queues and priv->rx_cfg.num_queues with priv->rx_cfg.max_queues in the statistics report length calculation.
intent_record.how: Ensures the allocated statistics report buffer size corresponds to the maximum configured queue capacity rather than the currently active queue count.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement writes to data[i++] without bounds checking on the index 'i'. When collecting multiple statistics, the index is incremented without validating against the allocated data array size, potentially causing buffer overflow if the caller provides insufficient output buffer space.

This statement continues the unsafe pattern of writing to data[i++] without bounds validation. Combined with subsequent increments, this contributes to potential buffer overflow when multiple statistics are collected.

This statement further increments the index 'i' without any bounds checking against the allocated data array size. The cumulative effect of multiple such increments without validation creates buffer overflow vulnerability.
